planning_notes: Wiring preserved: button signal uses Uno D2 to pushbutton terminal 1.r with pushbutton terminal 2.l to GND; this is configured as a pull-up input where the model value is true when pressed (pressed -> LOW -> model true).
Wiring preserved: LED anode/cathode connections route through resistor1 (pin D13 to resistor input) and LED to GND; configured as D13 digital output active-high (model true -> LED ON).
No serial input/output or other sensors/actuators are specified by the circuit; therefore no serial_channels are created.
Control-period is chosen as 5 ms for responsive button monitoring; exact debounce/edge-vs-level behavior is a model concern (not part of these port definitions).

interfaces.name: io_0
interfaces.meaning: Button pressed state (model value true when pressed; reads LOW on press with pull-up)

interfaces.name: io_1
interfaces.meaning: LED on while button is pressed (model true drives LED ON)

# Button Controlled LED

## Project Description
This is a Arduino project that controls an LED with a pushbutton. The LED will turn on only while the button is pressed and turn off when released.

## Hardware Components
- Arduino Uno
- Push Button
- 220Ω resistor
- LED

## Circuit Description
The circuit consists of:
- A pushbutton connected to a digital pin.
- An LED connected to a digital output pin through a 220Ω current-limiting resistor
- The cathode (negative leg) of the LED is connected to ground

## Expected Behavior
When the Arduino powers up, it should:
1. Configure the button pin as INPUT
2. Configure the LED pin as OUTPUT
3. Continuously monitor the button state
4. Turn the LED ON when the button is pressed (reads LOW)
5. Turn the LED OFF when the button is released (reads HIGH)

## Success Criteria
The test is successful when:
1. The LED turns on immediately when the button is pressed
2. The LED remains on only while the button is held down
3. The LED turns off immediately when the button is released

## Notes for Implementation
- The button input will read LOW when pressed if using a pull-up resistor configuration
- Ensure proper current-limiting resistor for the LED based on its specifications
- When the button is not pressed, pin1.l is connected to pin1.r and pin2.l is connected to pin2.r. When the button is pressed, all the pins are connected together.

## Attributes
- To use 220Ω resistor, set the property name "value" to "220 ohm".
Given circuit (must preserve wiring):
{
    "version": 1.0,
    "author": "Blind Author",
    "editor": "Blind Author",
    "description": "Button LED",
    "parts": [
        {
            "id": "arduino uno1",
            "type": "wokwi-arduino-uno",
            "top": 200,
            "left": 20
        },
        {
            "id": "resistor1",
            "type": "wokwi-resistor",
            "top": 75,
            "left": 115,
            "rotate": 90,
            "attrs": {
                "value": "220"
            }
        },
        {
            "id": "push button1",
            "type": "wokwi-pushbutton",
            "top": 125,
            "left": 180,
            "rotate": 90
        },
        {
            "id": "led1",
            "type": "wokwi-led",
            "left": 120,
            "top": 0,
            "attrs": {
                "color": "red"
            }
        }
    ],
    "connections": [
        [
            "arduino uno1:GND.1",
            "led1:C",
            "black",
            []
        ],
        [
            "resistor1:1",
            "led1:A",
            "green",
            []
        ],
        [
            "arduino uno1:13",
            "resistor1:2",
            "green",
            [
                "*",
                "h0"
            ]
        ],
        [
            "arduino uno1:2",
            "push button1:1.r",
            "red",
            [
                "v-12",
                "*",
                "h0"
            ]
        ],
        [
            "arduino uno1:GND.1",
            "push button1:2.l",
            "red",
            [
                "v-95",
                "*",
                "h0"
            ]
        ]
    ]
}
